Package net.sourceforge.plantuml.teavm.js.browser

Class PlantUMLBrowser

java.lang.Object
net.sourceforge.plantuml.teavm.js.browser.PlantUMLBrowser
public class PlantUMLBrowser extends Object
PlantUML rendering engine for browser environments, compiled to a JavaScript ES2015 module via TeaVM.

Overview

This class provides a bridge between JavaScript code running in a browser and the PlantUML Java rendering engine. The compiled output (plantuml.js) is an ES2015 module that exports two functions: render and renderToString.

Usage from JavaScript

 <script type="module">
   import { render, renderToString } from './plantuml.js';

   // Render directly into a DOM element
   const source = "@startuml\nAlice -> Bob : hello\n@enduml";
   const lines = source.split(/\r\n|\r|\n/);
   render(lines, "diagram-output-id");

   // Or get the SVG as a string
   renderToString(lines,
     svg => console.log(svg),
     err => console.error(err)
   );
 </script>
Both functions accept an optional options object as the last argument, e.g. { dark: true } to enable dark-mode rendering, or { maxSvgSize: 9999 } to raise the maximum SVG width/height (in pixels) beyond the default of 8192. Passing { maxSvgSize: 0 } disables the size check entirely.

Architecture: JavaScript-driven paradigm

The design follows a "JS-driven" architecture where:
  • JavaScript handles: UI events, user input, debouncing, line splitting, DOM element selection, and overall application flow
  • Java handles: PlantUML parsing and SVG rendering only
This separation keeps the Java code minimal and allows maximum flexibility for web developers to integrate PlantUML however they want.

No thread, no coroutine

There is no worker thread, and nothing in the engine suspends (no TeaVM coroutine: see tools/teavm-coroutines). What the rendering needs from JavaScript and can only get asynchronously (the Viz.js instance, support scripts such as emoji.js or <lib>.min.js, files of PLANTUML_FILE_LOADER) is handled by rendering again: an attempt that misses one is discarded, the resources are loaded with JavaScript callbacks, and the diagram is rendered again from its source (see PendingResources and RenderQueue).

The exported functions only queue the request and return: the rendering starts from a later JavaScript task (setTimeout), as it did when a worker thread did it, so the callbacks are never called before the function returns.

Order of the answers

Requests are answered one at a time, oldest first. Two rules decide what happens when several are waiting:
  • renderToString: every request is kept and answered, in the order received. Each of its callbacks is called exactly once (onSuccess or onError); a host that renders many diagrams at the same time gets all of them back.
  • render: only the latest request is kept, a new one replaces the render request still waiting, including one waiting for its resources. This is intentional: when a user is typing, we only care about rendering the latest version.
Neither kind drops the other. A callback that throws, or a missing callback, does not stop the engine. A request made from a callback (or while a request waits for its resources) is queued behind the ones already waiting: it is never rendered in the middle of another one.

The DOM element of render is only written with the result of the attempt that is kept, so a discarded attempt never shows.

  • Method Details

    • render

      public static void render(String[] lines, String elementId, org.teavm.jso.JSObject options)
      Renders a PlantUML diagram into the DOM element identified by elementId.

      This call is asynchronous: it returns immediately, and the SVG is inserted later, once its turn has come and its resources are there (see the class documentation).

      If a previous render request is still waiting, it is replaced by this one, and its diagram is never drawn. This is the desired behavior for live-typing scenarios. Waiting renderToString requests are not affected.

      Parameters:
      lines - the PlantUML source code, split into lines by the JavaScript caller
      elementId - the id of the HTML element where the SVG should be rendered
      options - optional JS object with rendering options (e.g. { dark: true, maxSvgSize: 8192 }); may be null. maxSvgSize overrides DEFAULT_MAX_SVG_SIZE; 0 disables the size check.

    • renderToString

      public static void renderToString(String[] lines, PlantUMLBrowser.StringCallback onSuccess, PlantUMLBrowser.StringCallback onError, org.teavm.jso.JSObject options)
      Renders a PlantUML diagram and delivers the resulting SVG as a string via the onSuccess callback. Errors go to onError.

      Same queueing and asynchronous behavior as render(java.lang.String[], java.lang.String, org.teavm.jso.JSObject): a callback is never called before this call returns. Unlike render(java.lang.String[], java.lang.String, org.teavm.jso.JSObject), requests are never dropped: each call is queued behind the ones already waiting, and exactly one of onSuccess and onError is called for it, once, in the order of the calls. A callback that is null or that throws does not stop the engine (an exception is reported with console.error).

      Parameters:
      lines - the PlantUML source code, split into lines by the JavaScript caller
      onSuccess - callback invoked with the SVG string when rendering succeeds
      onError - callback invoked with an error message when rendering fails
      options - optional JS object with rendering options (e.g. { dark: true, maxSvgSize: 8192 }); may be null. maxSvgSize overrides DEFAULT_MAX_SVG_SIZE; 0 disables the size check.
